The round of fixes that beta.8 held back, plus everything the reports since then pointed at. Sixteen changes, all from the mod database listing, the Discord and the review queue.

## Launching the game

**A missing .NET runtime is now named.** A game version built against a .NET major version you have not installed never starts, and until now the launcher said "Vintage Story exited with errors!", the same line a normal session gets. Lady Elayne's log on CachyOS had the real reason sitting in it: the game wanted .NET 10 and the machine had 8.0.29. The launcher now recognises the .NET host's own sentence on stderr and shows a message that says which dependency is missing, with a button that opens the install guide for your OS. Nothing the game printed reaches the screen, only a fixed message. To be clear for Steam Deck and other immutable systems, where PatoviiNet asked: .NET is the game's dependency, not the launcher's. The Linux guide now says so up front.

**Copied installations load the right mods.** An installation brought over from another launcher, or from a standalone Vintage Story data folder, carries a `clientsettings.json` whose mod folder list still points at the old folder, so the game loaded mods from the old install while the launcher managed the new one. At launch the launcher now repoints that list when it has the game's default shape and points elsewhere. A customised list is never touched, and the log says which of the two happened. Reported by AlexanderwithaA. `serverconfig.json` is still a manual edit.

## Mods

**The Install Mod compatibility verdict is readable.** The colour that was supposed to say whether a release matches your game version never reached the screen: the button it was on already set its own text colour and won. The verdict now sits on an element that keeps it, with a short word beside the icon (Tagged, Likely, Untagged) so it does not depend on colour at all. The supported game versions are plain wrapping text instead of a read-only field that clipped the list.

**Modpack import says what it is about to do.** NekoJess exported a 200-mod pack for a friend and read an import table of nothing but mod ids, which is why she thought the launcher was pulling in a mod she had never installed. The export now carries each mod's display name, the import table shows it, and every row says whether it will install, update, downgrade or leave the mod alone before anything happens. Three mods that are not on the database under their id are named as such instead of silently skipped.

**Manage Mods no longer starves other pages.** A large Mods folder queried the database once per installed mod with no cap, and a catalog search or a filter change on another page waited behind the whole scan. The scan is now bounded at two lookups at a time, leaving the rest of the shared budget to whatever page you are actually on.

## Notifications and the Activity Center

A full pass over everything you read as a notification, driven by an audit that is in the repository with a file and line on every finding.

**Bursts arrive on time.** Five errors fired together took 40 seconds to drain, the fifth landing 32 seconds after the event, and a modpack import raised one completion toast per mod into a queue that shows one at a time. A toast with something waiting behind it now gets a two second turn, the queue keeps at most four behind the one on screen, and the one on screen is never dropped whatever arrives. Five errors fired in the same instant now put the last one up inside nine seconds; spread over a couple of seconds, a burst of six drains in about 25 seconds instead of 48, because the banner already up and the last one still get their full turn. The modpack import uses the aggregate feedback the bulk updater always had.

**Hovering or focusing a toast holds it.** Reading a long message, or tabbing to its buttons, no longer races the countdown.

**Failed rows are readable.** The failure line in the Activity Center read 1.97:1 on a bright background, the least readable text in the panel on the one line you have to read. It and the error toast icon move to 5.70:1, and every notification colour is now held to its floor by a test.

**Mod downloads complete.** Arcanum3000 reported downloads stuck on "finalizing" for the whole session while the files landed fine. A progress tick arriving after the task had already completed was flipping it back to running. A finished task now stays finished.

**Keyboard.** Opening the Activity Center moves focus into it, so Tab stays in the panel and Escape closes it.

**Wording.** No more "Click here" on toasts that have a button, no exclamation mark on anything that reaches a notification, a backup row that no longer says the same fact three times, one duplicated word and one typo in a key fixed.

## Reliability

**A page that crashes no longer blanks the app.** Beta.7's blank Manage Mods took three reports to trace because nothing was written anywhere. A render error in one page now shows a message with a way back, keeps the shell running, and lands in `error.log` with a fixed-shape record: no raw messages, no stack text, only what a bug report needs.

**Login failures log a classified reason.** The one place where a password, a two-factor code and a token are all in scope logged whatever the failing code said. It now logs a fixed token for the cause and never the message.

**Background picks land in order.** Choosing a large scene and then a small one while the first was downloading saved the first one. Only the last pick applies.

**An interrupted restore is cleaned up.** A backup restore killed mid-extraction left a full game tree beside the installation that the startup sweep never reached. It does now, and the two cache sweeps share one walk and one bound.

**Dragging page text into a field does nothing.** Reported by AlexanderwithaA; text stays selectable and copyable.

## Known issues

The Windows installer is not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen and some antivirus tools warn on a fresh install. Every build here is produced by GitHub from the public source and you can check any file on VirusTotal before running it.

macOS still has no build.
